deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page: no formulas, computations or derivations. It is a heavily corrected draft of Riemann's speculative natural philosophy (the 'Geistesmassen' / Erdseele fragments, close to Fechner's ideas). It continues the previous page's application of the laws of mental processes to the purposiveness and history of organic nature on Earth. The argument runs as follows.

(a) The souls of plants growing in a climatically similar region enter the Earth-soul (Erdseele) and fuse there into one overall impression. This parallels the way the various sense perceptions of a single object merge in our soul into one image. In this way the totality of plants gives the Earth-soul a picture of the climatic and chemical state of the Earth's surface. This explains how the plan for later creations developed in the Earth's mental life.

(b) To satisfy our need for explanation, the mere persistence of Geistesmassen is not enough. Combination, at least of heterogeneous Geistesmassen, happens not directly but via Geistesmassen produced in a common nerve-like tissue. So the Earth-soul needs a material substrate.

(c) For reasons to be developed later, the seat of mental activity can only be sought in ponderable matter. The rigid crust demonstrably does not serve a common mental process; its motions must be explained otherwise.

(d) Directly beneath the solidified crust, all conditions known to be required for a soul-process appear to be met. Point 1: for the motions of dissolved matter to be governed by internal processes, the substances must be in a state where heat governs the relative position of their parts. This takes place in organic matter. Under the crust it must occur to a higher degree than organic arrangements on the surface can achieve. Point 2, an objection ('Bedenken'): on the whole Earth surface only the four organic elements (C, H, N, O) carry organic life.

The next page rebuts this objection: the conditions are only relative to present surface conditions. It then asks why these four elements are privileged, citing their resistance to condensation and the variety and easy decomposability of their compounds.
errors: No mathematical errors are possible, since there is no mathematics. The physical premises are speculative or obsolete by modern standards: an Earth-soul, a living molten zone under the crust, and the four 'permanent' elements as hard-to-condense gases (H, N, O were later liquefied in 1877–1898; carbon is not a gas). These are historical views, not slips.

results.what: Hypothesis of an Earth-soul integrating the souls of organisms, with plants furnishing an image of the climate and chemistry of the surface
Locating the material seat of the Earth's mental activity in the hot zone directly beneath the solid crust, where heat controls the relative position of particles
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's own speculation in his philosophical fragments (partially printed in Weber–Dedekind, Gesammelte Werke, 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts')

deep.surprise_reason: Purely philosophical and speculative text. Riemann's Fechner-inspired psychology and metaphysics, including the Erdseele, is known from the published philosophical fragments. This draft adds only minor unpublished wording and argumentative detail, and contains no mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: likely 'Gegend der Erdoberfläche in die Erdseele eintreten'; the struck word is 'Zeit', and 'in die' precedes 'Erdseele'.

'Auf diese Weise erklärt es sich, wie ...': the insertion above appears to read '(im) Seelen(leben) der Erde', i.e. 'wie im Seelenleben der Erde sich der Plan zu den späteren Schöpfungen entwickelte'.
'Aber um unserem Erklärungsbedürfnisse [zu] genügen, bedarf es [nicht blos] des Fortbestehens verschiedener Geistesmassen ...': the reading of the middle of this sentence is uncertain.

Point 1 marginal insertion: roughly 'Stoffe ... [in einem Zustande sein, in welchem die] Wirkung der Wärme auf die relative Lage ihrer Theile [überwiegt]'. The bracketed words are a reconstruction from context and the next page.
Point 2: 'Bedenken' is inserted above 'Hauptgrund', perhaps as an alternative ('Als Hauptbedenken gegen diese Annahme scheint die Thatsache zu sein ...').
